behaviors.name: Workflow
behaviors.description: A state machine on the instance: a status that starts in the initial state and changes only through transition, along a transition the config lists. A transition may name a permission the caller must hold. A state that no transition leaves is terminal, and a terminal state has an outcome: success, failure or neutral, success unless the config says otherwise. Other instances' blockers, rollups and reactions read it.
behaviors.summary: Its status is one of queued, running, done and failed; a new Job starts in queued, and status moves only by transition. Terminal, with their outcomes: done (success) and failed (success).

fields.description: The state the instance is in.

behaviors.name: Lease
behaviors.description: An exclusive, time-bounded lease on the instance, held by one principal and numbered by a fencing token that advances at every acquire, release and expiry. While the lease is active only its holder may change the instance, and a write that presents a token other than the current one, as Lease's precondition, is refused whoever calls; a heartbeat with the current token renews the lease and delivers the directives sent to the holder. A lease its holder stops renewing expires, and the expiry can move the instance's Workflow status back.
behaviors.summary: A lease gives one principal the Job for 1 minute at a time, renewed by heartbeat at least every 20 seconds. The runner expires a lapsed lease within 5 seconds. While a lease is active only its holder writes; each acquire gives a new token, which the holder presents as preconditions {"Lease": {"token": n}}.

behaviors.name: Assignment
behaviors.description: Assigns the instance to one principal at a time. A principal may assign an unassigned instance to itself and unassign itself; assigning another principal, reassigning, and unassigning another principal need the config's permission. While the instance is assigned, only its assignee may take its lease (Lease's acquire) or claim it (Queue's claim).
behaviors.summary: Each Job is assigned to one principal or none; while it is assigned, only its assignee acquires its lease or claims it. A principal assigns an unassigned instance to itself and unassigns itself; the config names no permission for anything else.

behaviors.name: Retries
behaviors.description: Retries per failure class. Each attempt is recorded with recordAttempt: a success, or a failure of a class the config names, which counts against that class's cap and a total cap. A terminal class, a failure past a cap, or the same failure signature repeated stuckAfter times exhausts the instance, and its Workflow status moves to exhaustedState from the config's from states through Workflow's transition. Once exhausted, its status moves only to exhaustedState and its lease cannot be taken. A kept result, the best scoring one when keepBest is given, is written to resultField with the checks of an update. There is no backoff in time. Requires Workflow.
behaviors.summary: Failure classes: flaky (1 attempt); at most 3 counted failures in all. Once exhausted, status moves from queued or running to failed, and the Job takes no more attempts, moves only to failed, and is not acquired or claimed.

The holder of the instance's active lease does not change limitsField: a worker never raises its own caps.
The config names no limitsPermission, so limitsField does not change once the instance exists.

operations.name: create
operations.title: Create Job
operations.description: Creates a Job: validates the instance, data, against the schema's live version and stores it under id, or under a new id when none is given.

id.description: The instance id; the engine makes one when it is absent

guidance.useWhen: Use to create a new Job: data holds its own fields, and id names it, or the engine makes one.
guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to change one that exists; call update.
guidance.success: Returns the new instance with its id, its seq, its own fields in data and its behaviors' fields in behaviors, by behavior name. A new instance's status is queued.

operations.name: get
operations.title: Get Job
operations.description: Returns the Job with the id: its own fields in data, its behaviors' in behaviors.

valueRefs.description: Return each field the value store holds as its ref, { "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }, listed in valueRefs, rather than its value, which get_value reads

guidance.useWhen: Use when you have the id of the Job to read.
guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to find Job instances; call list.
guidance.success: Returns the instance with its seq, its own fields in data and its behaviors' fields in behaviors, by behavior name.

operations.name: list
operations.title: List Job
operations.description: Lists Job instances in creation order, a page at a time: pass a page's next as cursor for the page after it. where keeps the instances whose fields hold the values it gives, a list meaning any of them; a filtered page can hold fewer than limit while next is not null.

limit.description: How many instances a page holds, 50 when absent

valueRefs.description: Return each field the value store holds as its ref, { "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }, listed in valueRefs, rather than its value, which get_value reads

where.description: The values the instances hold, by field: a value, null for none, or a list of 1 to 100 meaning any of them; every member must hold

anyOf.description: The state the instance is in.

items.description: The state the instance is in.

anyOf.description: The principal that holds its lease, a lapsed one included until its expiry is applied; null for a free instance.

items.description: The principal that holds its lease, a lapsed one included until its expiry is applied; null for a free instance.

anyOf.description: The principal the instance is assigned to; absent when it is unassigned.

items.description: The principal the instance is assigned to; absent when it is unassigned.

next.description: The next page's cursor; null after the last page

guidance.useWhen: Use to page through Job instances, oldest first. where keeps the ones whose fields hold the values it gives, null meaning no value and a list of values any of them: title, priority, timeLimitMs, topic, urgent, Workflow.status, Lease.holder, Assignment.assignee or Retries.exhausted; a behavior's field by its qualified name, the behavior's, a dot and the field's. where: { "Workflow.status": <state> } lists the instances in one of queued, running, done or failed, and a list of states the instances in any of them. where: { "Lease.holder": <subject> } lists the Job instances whose lease a principal holds, a lapsed one until the runner expires it, and "Lease.holder": null the free ones. where: { "Assignment.assignee": <subject> } lists the Job instances assigned to a principal, "Assignment.assignee": null the unassigned ones, and [null, <subject>] both. where: { "Retries.exhausted": true } lists the Job instances whose retries are exhausted, and false the ones that may run again.
guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read one instance whose id you have; call get.
guidance.success: Returns items and next; pass next as cursor for the page after, until it is null. With where, a page can hold fewer items than limit, even none, while next is not null: read on until it is.

operations.name: update
operations.title: Update Job
operations.description: Applies a JSON merge patch (RFC 7386) to the Job with the id: a member replaces the instance's, a nested object merges and null removes a member. With expectedSeq the update is refused unless the instance is still at that sequence.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

patch.description: A JSON merge patch of the Job

guidance.useWhen: Use to change the own fields of the Job with the id, as a JSON merge patch; with expectedSeq, the update is refused if the instance changed since that seq.
guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to set a behavior's field: the patch holds own fields only, and a behavior's fields change only through its operations. Do not use to move Workflow's status, which behaviors.Workflow holds; call transition. Do not write under another principal's active lease; the holder may present its token as preconditions {"Lease": {"token": n}}, which a newer lease makes stale.
guidance.success: Returns the instance as the patch left it, with its next seq.

operations.name: delete
operations.title: Delete Job
operations.description: Deletes the Job with the id. With expectedSeq the delete is refused unless the instance is still at that sequence.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

guidance.useWhen: Use to delete the Job with the id for good; with expectedSeq, the delete is refused if the instance changed since that seq.
guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not write under another principal's active lease; the holder may present its token as preconditions {"Lease": {"token": n}}, which a newer lease makes stale.
guidance.success: Returns null; the instance and what its behaviors kept for it are gone.

operations.name: transition
operations.title: Job: transition
operations.description: Moves the instance to another state along a transition the config lists. A transition that names a permission needs a caller who holds it.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

from.description: The state the instance was in.

to.description: The state it is in now.

guidance.useWhen: Use to move status from queued to running or failed; from running to queued, done or failed.
guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use from done or failed: no transition leaves a terminal state. Do not use to stay where the instance is. Do not write under another principal's active lease; the holder may present its token as preconditions {"Lease": {"token": n}}, which a newer lease makes stale. Do not move an exhausted instance anywhere but failed.
guidance.success: Returns from and to; status holds to from then on, and enteredAt the time of the move.

operations.name: acquire
operations.title: Job: acquire
operations.description: Takes the lease for the caller and returns its fencing token. Refused while a lease is active, the caller's own included (heartbeat renews it), without acquirePermission when the config names one, and once the instance has had maxExpiries expiries. Over a lease that expired, it applies that expiry first.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

ttlMs.description: How long the lease lasts after its acquire and each heartbeat, in milliseconds, at most the config's ttlMs; the config's when absent.

expiresAt.description: When the lease expires unless renewed, in epoch milliseconds.

heartbeatMs.description: How often to send a heartbeat, in milliseconds.

token.description: The lease's fencing token, which the holder's writes present as Lease's precondition.

guidance.useWhen: Use to take the lease, for 1 minute or a shorter ttlMs, before working on the instance alone.
guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use on an instance assigned to another principal. Do not use once behaviors.Retries.exhausted is true.
guidance.success: Returns token, expiresAt and heartbeatMs: heartbeat at least every heartbeatMs and present the token as preconditions {"Lease": {"token": n}} on each write.

errors.description: Lease: Another principal holds the instance's active lease.
errors.commonCorrection: Wait until expiresAt in details, or work on another instance.

errors.description: Lease: The caller already holds the active lease: acquire refuses it, and heartbeat renews it.
errors.commonCorrection: Keep the lease you hold: renew it with heartbeat.

errors.description: Lease: The token the call presents as Lease's precondition is not the lease's current one: a newer lease, or none, has replaced the one it names.
errors.commonCorrection: Stop: a newer lease replaced yours. Read behaviors.Lease, and acquire again only if it is free.

errors.description: Assignment: The instance is assigned to another principal, who alone may acquire its lease or claim it.
errors.commonCorrection: Take work assigned to you or to no one, or have it unassigned first.

errors.description: Retries: The instance's retries are exhausted: it takes no more attempts, its status moves only to exhaustedState, and it is not acquired or claimed again.
errors.commonCorrection: None: the instance takes no more attempts; create new work instead.

operations.name: heartbeat
operations.title: Job: heartbeat
operations.description: Renews the lease, never past its longest hold, acknowledges the directives acknowledge names, and returns the directives sent under it that are not acknowledged. Only the holder, presenting the current token as Lease's precondition, while the lease is active: an expired lease cannot be renewed.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

acknowledge.description: Directives of the lease to mark handled first, as acknowledge does, so a heartbeat acknowledges in the same write; empty, none.

directives.description: The directives sent under this lease and not acknowledged, oldest first.

dedupeKey.description: The key it was sent with, when it was.

id.description: The directive's number in its lease.

expiresAt.description: When the lease now expires unless renewed, in epoch milliseconds.

guidance.useWhen: Use as the holder at least every 20 seconds, presenting the token, to keep the lease; acknowledge takes the ids of directives handled.
guidance.success: Returns the new expiresAt and the directives not yet acknowledged, oldest first.

operations.name: release
operations.title: Job: release
operations.description: Ends an active lease: the holder, presenting the current token as Lease's precondition, or a principal with overridePermission, who need not. The token advances, so the directives sent under the lease are not delivered again, and onExpiry moves the status when it is still one of its from states. With abandon, the holder gives the work up as failed: the release counts as an expiry, and escalate applies at the one that reaches maxExpiries.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

abandon.description: Whether the work is given up as failed, so the release counts as an expiry.

guidance.useWhen: Use as the holder, presenting the token, when done with the instance or handing it back. abandon true gives it up as failed, which counts as an expiry.
guidance.success: Returns {}; the lease is free and its token stale.

operations.name: expire
operations.title: Job: expire
operations.description: Applies the expiry of a lease past its expiry time or its longest hold: the holder is cleared, the token advances, the expiry is counted unless the instance is in a terminal state of its Workflow, and onExpiry or escalate moves the status. Any principal who may write the instance may call it; on any other instance it changes nothing. With holder, a principal with overridePermission expires that holder's lease at once, active or not, unless notRenewedAfter spares it. The engine's runner calls it on every lapsed lease, every sweepMs.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

holder.description: The principal whose lease to expire now, active or not; it needs overridePermission.

notRenewedAfter.description: With holder: an active lease its holder acquired or renewed after this time, in epoch milliseconds, is spared, since its own heartbeats show the process holding it is alive. A lapsed one expires all the same.

reason.description: Why, when one expired: ttl, its holder stopped renewing it; maxHold, it reached its longest hold; holder, it was active and expired by its holder's name.

guidance.useWhen: Use to apply the expiry of a lapsed lease; the runner's sweep does so within 5 seconds.
guidance.success: Returns expired and its reason: ttl, maxHold or holder.

operations.name: direct
operations.title: Job: direct
operations.description: Sends the holder of the active lease a directive, which its heartbeats deliver until it acknowledges it. With dedupeKey, a directive already sent under the lease with the key is not sent again. A principal needs directPermission, or overridePermission when that is absent, and is refused when the config names neither; another behavior of the type sends one with call(), as the principal it runs for, without either.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

dedupeKey.description: Sends the directive once per lease: when one was sent under the current token with this key, acknowledged or not, that one stands and nothing is sent.

created.description: Whether this call sent it; false when one with dedupeKey was already sent.

id.description: The directive's number in its lease: the one sent, or the one already sent with dedupeKey.

guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use: the config names no permission that sends directives.
guidance.success: Returns the directive id, and created false when one with its dedupeKey stands.

errors.description: Lease: No principal holds a lease on the instance.
errors.commonCorrection: Acquire the lease (or claim the instance) first.

errors.description: Lease: The lease is past its expiry time or its longest hold: it gives its holder nothing, and only its expiry can follow.
errors.commonCorrection: Stop working on the instance: the lease has lapsed. Acquire it again once it has expired.

errors.description: Lease: The config names no permission that allows the call: direct without directPermission or overridePermission, resetExpiries without overridePermission.
errors.commonCorrection: None: the type's Lease config names no permission that allows it.

operations.name: acknowledge
operations.title: Job: acknowledge
operations.description: Marks directives of the lease as handled, so heartbeats stop delivering them. Only the holder, presenting the current token as Lease's precondition.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

guidance.useWhen: Use as the holder, presenting the token, to stop directives' delivery; heartbeat's acknowledge does the same in the heartbeat's write.

operations.name: expireHolder
operations.title: Job: expireHolder
operations.description: Expires every lease one principal holds on the schema's instances, active or not, as expire with that holder does on each: for a principal that is gone. With notRenewedAfter, an active lease renewed after that time is spared. Needs overridePermission; refused when the config names none.

holder.description: The principal whose leases to expire.

notRenewedAfter.description: As expire's: an active lease acquired or renewed after this time is spared.

ids.description: The instances whose lease expired, by id.

reasons.description: How many expired for each reason expire gives, by reason; a reason none expired for is absent.

guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use: the config names no overridePermission, which it needs.

operations.name: resetExpiries
operations.title: Job: resetExpiries
operations.description: Sets the instance's count of expiries back to 0, so a lease can be acquired again after maxExpiries. Needs overridePermission; refused when the config names none.

guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use: the config names no overridePermission, which it needs.

errors.description: Lease: The config names no permission that allows the call: direct without directPermission or overridePermission, resetExpiries without overridePermission.
errors.commonCorrection: None: the type's Lease config names no permission that allows it.

operations.name: assign
operations.title: Job: assign
operations.description: Assigns the instance to a principal: the caller itself when it is unassigned, or anyone, reassigning included, with the config's permission.

operations.name: recordAttempt
operations.title: Job: recordAttempt
operations.description: Records an attempt: a success without failure, or a failure of one of the config's classes, counted against its caps, and returns the class's hint. Decides whether its result is kept, and writes a kept result to resultField. Exhausts the instance at a terminal class, a failure past a cap or a stuck signature, moving its status to exhaustedState from the from states. Refused once the instance is exhausted, and without the config's permission.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

detail.description: Anything about the attempt worth keeping, such as validation errors: recorded in the operation's event and nowhere else.

failure.description: The failure class; a success when absent.

predicates.description: Named checks the attempt passed or failed, for keepBest's neverRegress; a predicate absent here counts as failed.

result.description: The attempt's result, written to resultField when it is kept; needs resultField.

score.description: The attempt's score; higher is better.

signature.description: What identifies the failure, for stuckAfter: the same signature in a row is the same failure.

classAttempts.description: Failures counted so far, by class.

failure.description: The failure class; null for a success.

hint.description: The failure class's hint; null for a success and a class without one.

kept.description: Whether the attempt's result was kept.

stuck.description: Whether a repeated signature exhausted the instance.

guidance.useWhen: Use after each attempt: without failure it is a success; with failure, one of flaky.
guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not write under another principal's active lease; the holder may present its token as preconditions {"Lease": {"token": n}}, which a newer lease makes stale.
guidance.success: Returns the counts, whether the instance is exhausted or stuck, and the failure class's hint for the next attempt.
